t: Yarlung kings united the Tibetan plateau in the 7th century and ruled it from Lhasa as divine emperors (tsenpo).
Its cavalry fought Tang China for the Tarim Basin and Hexi Corridor, and briefly occupied Chang'an in 763.
It gave Tibet its script and made Buddhism the religion of the court, founding Samye monastery around 779.
dyk: The peace treaty Tibet swore with Tang China in 821–822 was carved in Tibetan and Chinese on a stone pillar that still stands in front of the Jokhang temple in Lhasa.
ev: Princess Wencheng of Tang China arrives as a bride for the Tibetan royal house
Tibet conquers the Tuyuhun around Lake Kokonor
Tibetans defeat a Tang army at the Dafei River and overrun the Tarim Basin
A Tibetan army occupies the Tang capital Chang'an for about two weeks
Tibet and Tang China swear a peace treaty, recorded on a pillar in Lhasa
Emperor Udumtsen (Langdarma) is assassinated and the empire breaks apart

f.capital: Lhasa; the court also moved between seasonal camps
f.founder: Namri Songtsen and his son Songtsen Gampo
f.successor: Era of Fragmentation (Guge and other Tibetan kingdoms)
